chapter.title: Scope
chapter.para: This document defines the web service interface for discovering and controlling storage resources available to an ONVIF device. The service supports local storage, removable media such as SD cards, and network storage resources. A device may expose more than one storage resource.
Web service usage and common ONVIF functionality are outside the scope of this document. Please refer to the ONVIF Core Specification for more information.

section.title: Conventions
section.para: The key words “shall”, “shall not”, “should”, “should not”, “may”, “need not”, “can”, and “cannot” in this specification are to be interpreted as described in Annex H of [ISO/IEC Directives].

entry.para: An independently addressable storage instance exposed by the device.
Storage media that can be physically inserted into and removed from the device, such as an SD card.
The percentage of estimated remaining usable media life.
A secret used by the device to protect encryption of a complete managed storage resource.

chapter.title: Overview
chapter.para: The Storage service provides a common resource model for storage that can be used for recording or other device functions. It provides resource discovery, capacity and health information, lifecycle operations, and storage events.

listitem.para: Querying storage capability and resource availability.
Retrieving capacity, usage, format, encryption, and wear information.
Setting or changing a storage encryption passphrase.
Using a storage token for recording.
Receiving storage lifecycle and operation events.

chapter.para: The WSDL for this service is specified in http://www.onvif.org/onvif/ver10/storage/wsdl/storage.wsdl.

section.title: Storage resources
section.para: Each storage resource is identified by a reference token. A device shall return a separate resource for each independently usable storage instance, including each inserted card in a device with multiple card slots.
The StorageType identifies the resource as Local, Removable, or Network.
A resource token shall remain stable while the corresponding resource remains associated with the device. A device may allocate a new token when a physically removed removable medium is replaced.

section.title: Storage information
section.para: The StorageInfo structure contains the resource type, state, and resource-specific capabilities. Capacity and used space shall be expressed in bytes. Available space may be omitted when the resource is not available. A device shall not report stale values as current values.
The state shall be one of Available, Mounted, Formatting, Reencrypting, Error, or Unknown.
The format identifies the manufacturer-specific format of the storage resource. The encryption information identifies the encryption state of the complete managed storage resource.
The Capabilities element shall specify, for the individual resource, whether formatting (Format), encryption (Encryption), and passphrase changes (PassphraseChange) are supported.
If wear information is supported, Wear shall express remaining media life as a percentage in the range 0.0 through 100.0. The element shall be omitted when the device cannot provide a value.

section.title: Capabilities
section.para: A device that exposes the Storage service shall implement GetServiceCapabilities. The response may indicate support for removable and network storage and may report the number of physical removable storage slots using RemovableStorageSlotCount. Formatting, encryption, and passphrase-change support shall be reported for each resource in its StorageInfo/Capabilities element.

section.title: Persistence
section.para: Storage resource configuration and encryption state shall survive a power cycle. The presence, capacity, usage, and operational state of removable and network resources may change during device operation.

chapter.title: Commands
chapter.para: This section describes the commands offered by the Storage service.

section.title: GetServiceCapabilities
section.para: This operation retrieves the capabilities of the Storage service.

listitem.para: The capabilities of the Storage service.

section.title: GetStorages
section.para: This operation lists all storage resources known to the service.

listitem.para: The storage resources known to the device.

section.title: GetStorage
section.para: This operation retrieves a storage resource whose token is known to the client.

listitem.para: The token of the requested storage resource.
The requested storage resource does not exist.

section.title: FormatStorage
section.para: This destructive operation formats the selected storage resource. The filesystem selected by the device is manufacturer-specific.

listitem.para: The token used to monitor the asynchronous operation.
The resource is absent, read-only, unavailable, locked, or in use.

section.para: The device shall not format a resource while active recording depends on it unless the device has first stopped or safely redirected that recording. Formatting shall be asynchronous whenever it cannot complete before the response is sent.

section.title: SetStoragePassphrase
section.para: This operation sets or changes the encryption passphrase for the complete managed storage resource.

listitem.para: The passphrases are write-only. CurrentPassphrase may be omitted only when encryption is enabled for the first time.
The token used to monitor re-encryption.
The resource or supplied passphrase is invalid, or a conflicting operation is active.

section.para: Changing a passphrase shall preserve readable existing data and shall re-encrypt the resource. The device shall never return a current or previous passphrase in a response, event, log, or storage information structure. Clients should use TLS.

section.title: GetOperationStatus
section.para: This operation retrieves the status of a formatting or re-encryption operation.

listitem.para: The current state, progress, and optional error information.

section.para: Operation progress is normalized between 0.0 and 1.0. The device shall report the final result through the standard Monitoring/AsynchronousOperationStatus event.

chapter.title: Recording Integration
chapter.para: A storage resource may be referenced by the Recording service using its token. The token is supplied in the recording configuration's StorageToken element.

chapter.title: Events
chapter.para: The Storage service shall dispatch the events defined in this chapter through the Event service. The events are limited to storage conditions that affect recording or require client action.

section.title: Storage status
section.para: When the status of a storage resource changes, the device shall dispatch the following event:
section.programlisting: Topic: tns1:Storage/Status <tt:MessageDescription IsProperty="true"> <tt:Source> <tt:SimpleItemDescription Name="StorageToken" Type="tt:ReferenceToken"/> </tt:Source> <tt:Data> <tt:SimpleItemDescription Name="Status" Type="ts:StorageStatus"/> </tt:Data> </tt:MessageDescription>
section.para: The status shall indicate whether the storage resource is available, needsFormatting, or has a wrongPassphrase.

section.title: Storage wear
section.para: When the wear value of a removable storage resource changes, the device shall dispatch the following event. The event shall not be repeatedly generated without a state change.
section.programlisting: Topic: tns1:Storage/Wear <tt:MessageDescription IsProperty="true"> <tt:Source> <tt:SimpleItemDescription Name="StorageToken" Type="tt:ReferenceToken"/> </tt:Source> <tt:Data> <tt:SimpleItemDescription Name="Wear" Type="xs:float"/> </tt:Data> </tt:MessageDescription>
section.para: The Wear value is the normalized remaining media life defined in the Storage information model.

section.title: Asynchronous storage operations
section.para: Formatting and passphrase changes shall use the standard asynchronous operation event defined by the Core Specification. The device shall dispatch progress, completion, cancellation, and failure notifications using the following topic:

For these operations, the ServiceName field shall identify the Storage service and the OperationName field shall be FormatStorage or SetStoragePassphrase. The Token field shall contain the operation token returned by the corresponding command. Progress shall be normalized between 0.0 and 1.0. Failures shall be reported in the Error field as defined by the Core Specification.
